e.meaning: from Massy, a place in northern France
e.etymology: A respelling of Macy, an English surname brought by Normans from Massy in northern France, a place named for a Gallo-Roman landowner called Maccius.
An Italian pet form of Carmela, from Mount Carmel in the Holy Land and the title Our Lady of Mount Carmel. Carmel is Hebrew for garden or orchard.
A respelling of Gracie, the pet form of Grace, the virtue name from Latin gratia.
A Latin variant of Viviana, probably from vivus, alive. Saint Bibiana was a Roman martyr of the fourth century.
A transposed spelling of Aidan that rose with it in the 2000s. Aidan anglicizes Irish Aodhán, a pet form of Aodh, fire.
The Polish, Slovak and Dutch form of Joseph, through Latin and Greek from Hebrew Yosef, he will add.
A respelling of Aidan, which anglicizes Irish Aodhán, a pet form of Aodh, fire. Saint Aidan founded the monastery of Lindisfarne in the seventh century.

e.meaning: from Laurentum, a city whose name is linked to laurel
e.etymology: A respelling of Lorenzo, the Italian and Spanish form of Laurence, from Latin Laurentius, a man from Laurentum.
The South Slavic and German form of Jasmine, the flower name that came through Arabic yasamin from Persian yasaman.
A spelling of Keira, an anglicized form of Irish Ciara, the feminine of Ciarán, from ciar, dark or black. It rose in the 2000s with actress Keira Knightley.
In Roman legend Remus was the twin of Romulus, raised by a she-wolf and killed in the quarrel over founding Rome. The origin of the name is unknown; it is in everyday use in Romania.
namesakes: Remus Lupin (werewolf professor in Harry Potter)
Uncle Remus (narrator of Joel Chandler Harris's folktales)

assoc.t: Remus Lupin, the werewolf professor in Harry Potter
twin of Romulus in Rome's founding legend

e.note: Uncle Remus, narrator of the 19th-century Brer Rabbit tales, is now widely seen as a racial stereotype.

e.etymology: A spelling of Tyree, a Scottish surname related to McIntyre that became an African-American first name in the 1970s. Tyrie is also a Scottish surname in its own right.
A modern blend of Angel or Angela with Elise.
Arabic ramzi, symbolic, from ramz, a symbol or sign.
A combination of Anna and Alicia. Anna is from Hebrew Hannah, grace; Alicia is the Latinized form of Alice, of noble kind.
The feminine of Miroslav, from Slavic mir, peace or world, and slava, glory. It has a following in Mexico, where the Czech-born film star Miroslava was famous in the 1950s.

e.meaning: one who has achieved his goal
e.etymology: A spelling of Siddharth, from Sanskrit siddha, accomplished, and artha, aim or purpose. Siddhartha was the birth name of the Buddha.
namesakes: Siddhartha Gautama (the Buddha, whose birth name this is)

e.etymology: A form of Salome, from Hebrew shalom, peace. Saloma is a long-standing name in Amish and Mennonite families.
A Latin American blend, usually of José with María or Mario, in the pattern of Jomar and Osmar.
From Cana in Galilee, where the Gospel of John sets the wedding at which Jesus turned water into wine. The place name is usually traced to Hebrew qaneh, reed.
A spelling of Lorelei, the rock on the Rhine whose name is read as murmuring rock, and the siren of German legend who sang sailors onto it.
A Scottish and northern English surname. As a first name it follows Vin Diesel's antihero Riddick, of Pitch Black and The Chronicles of Riddick, and boxer Riddick Bowe.

assoc.t: Vin Diesel's antihero in The Chronicles of Riddick

e.etymology: Sanskrit devika, a diminutive of devi, goddess.
An African-American coinage that joins the Ja- prefix to Amir, Arabic for prince or commander; usually spelled Jamir.
A phonetic spelling of Mekhi, the name made familiar by actor Mekhi Phifer; it also overlaps with Makai.
A modern spelling of Samaya or Samiyah. Samiyah is Arabic for elevated or sublime; Samaya is also a Sanskrit word for an appointed time or vow.

e.meaning: uncertain; perhaps son (Basque) or one who hears (from Simon)
e.etymology: A spelling of Jimena or Ximena, the feminine of the medieval Spanish name Ximeno, which may come from Basque seme, son, or be a form of Simon. Jimena was the wife of El Cid.
A short, punchy name best known from Taz, the Looney Tunes Tasmanian Devil, whose cartoon series Taz-Mania began in 1991. It is also a nickname for longer names such as Tazewell.

assoc.t: Taz, the Looney Tunes Tasmanian Devil

e.etymology: Arabic hammad, one who gives much praise to God, an intensive form from the same root as Hamad, Ahmad and Muhammad.
The German form of Henry, from Old High German Heimrih, made of heim, home, and rih, ruler. Seven German kings bore it.
namesakes: Heinrich Hertz (physicist who proved radio waves exist)
e.note: Many Americans know the name mainly from Heinrich Himmler, head of the Nazi SS.

e.etymology: A boys' name of Urdu-speaking Muslim families, most common in Pakistan.
A Spanish phonetic spelling of the English word lady, popular in Colombia and Central America since the 1980s, the era of Lady Diana; also written Leidy.
